The present invention is directed to a method, apparatus and computer-readable medium for utilizing a shared computer system. The method may also include processing, utilizing at least one processor, the access request. The system may also include determining, based on the processed access request, a classification of the potential user with respect to one or more potential or actual access rights to be associated with the potential user for accessing the secure data processing center. In the method, the determined classification of the potential user is that the potential user is at least one of a non-user, an eligible user, a limited user and an authorized user of the secure data processing center. In the method, the determining includes identifying whether the potential user is associated with an entity that is at least one of a financial entity, a health care entity, a national security entity, a law enforcement entity an educational entity or a combination thereof.

outputs.L1: The present invention is directed to a method, apparatus, and computer-readable medium for utilizing a shared computer system. The method includes receiving, through at least one interface, an access request associated with a potential user seeking access to a secure data processing center. The method may further include processing the access request using at least one processor and determining, based on the processed access request, a classification of the potential user with respect to one or more potential or actual access rights to be associated with the potential user for accessing the secure data processing center. The determined classification identifies the potential user as at least one of a non-user, an eligible user, a limited user, or an authorized user of the secure data processing center. The determining includes identifying whether the potential user is associated with an entity that is at least one of a financial entity, a health care entity, a national security entity, a law enforcement entity, an educational entity, or a combination thereof.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a technique, system, and computer-readable storage medium for operating a shared computing environment. Through one or more interfaces, a request is received from or relating to a prospective user who seeks entry to a secure data-processing center. At least one processor may then evaluate the request. Based on the evaluation, the prospective user is assigned a category reflecting one or more possible or existing access privileges for the secure center. The assigned category identifies the person as a non-user, eligible user, limited user, authorized user, or any applicable combination of these classifications. This determination includes establishing whether the prospective user is affiliated with a financial, healthcare, national-security, law-enforcement, or educational organization, or with any combination of such organizations.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a method, an apparatus, and a computer-readable medium for facilitating the use of a shared computer system. An interface receives a request from a potential user seeking access to a secure data processing center. At least one processor evaluates the request to determine the potential or actual access rights of the requesting user.

Based on this evaluation, the processor classifies the potential user as a non-user, an eligible user, a limited user, or an authorized user. In determining the appropriate classification, the processor may consider whether the user is associated with a financial institution, health care organization, national security agency, law enforcement organization, educational institution, or an entity that combines two or more of these functions. The resulting classification may then be used to control the scope and level of access granted to the shared computer system and its secure data processing resources.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to controlling access to a shared, secure data processing center used by multiple individuals, organizations, or other entities. In particular, the invention provides a method, an apparatus, and a non-transitory computer-readable medium for receiving, evaluating, and processing user access requests through an interface coupled to one or more processors.

When a person or entity requests access, the interface receives identification, affiliation, credential, and other relevant information associated with the request. The processor evaluates that information according to predetermined eligibility rules and security criteria. At least part of the evaluation may concern whether the requesting party is affiliated with an entity operating in, supporting, regulating, or otherwise connected to a sensitive sector. Sensitive sectors may include, for example, government, defense, intelligence, critical infrastructure, financial services, healthcare, communications, energy, or other fields for which unauthorized access could create elevated security, privacy, operational, or regulatory risks.

Based on the evaluation, the processor assigns the requesting party to one of several access classifications. A non-user may be a party that has not established a recognized relationship with the data processing center or that does not satisfy minimum identification or eligibility requirements. An eligible user may satisfy preliminary requirements but may still be required to complete registration, authentication, approval, training, or another onboarding procedure before obtaining access. A limited user may receive access only to specified systems, datasets, applications, functions, time periods, or physical or logical areas. An authorized user may receive broader access consistent with the user’s approved role, demonstrated need, security clearance, contractual status, and organizational affiliation.

The assigned classification is used to determine and enforce corresponding access rights. The processor may grant a request, deny the request, restrict the requested access, require additional authentication, or route the request for manual review. Access controls may be applied at different levels, including the facility, network, computing platform, application, service, dataset, record, or individual operation. The system may also impose conditions such as multifactor authentication, device verification, geographic restrictions, time-based limitations, session monitoring, enhanced logging, data-transfer controls, or periodic reauthorization.

Affiliation with a sensitive-sector entity may affect both eligibility and the degree of security scrutiny applied to the request. For example, such an affiliation may establish a legitimate basis for access while also triggering stronger identity verification, conflict checks, segregation requirements, supervisory approval, or continuous monitoring. The classification process may consider additional factors, including the reliability of submitted credentials, prior access history, current employment or contractual status, the sensitivity of the requested resources, applicable laws and policies, and detected security risks.

The system may update a user’s classification when relevant circumstances change. A user may be promoted from eligible user to authorized user after completing required approval steps, reduced to limited-user status when a role changes, or reclassified as a non-user when an affiliation ends or credentials expire. Access may also be suspended or revoked in response to anomalous activity, policy violations, failed authentication attempts, or newly identified security concerns. Classification decisions and resulting access actions may be recorded in an audit log to support compliance, investigation, reporting, and review.

An apparatus implementing the invention may include a communication interface, memory, and one or more processors. The memory stores instructions, user records, affiliation information, access policies, classification criteria, and audit information. When executing the stored instructions, the processor receives an access request, obtains or verifies information associated with the requester, determines the requester’s classification, identifies the access rights corresponding to that classification, and causes the requested access to be granted, limited, denied, or subjected to additional controls.

The invention may also be embodied in a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause a computing system to perform the described operations. The medium may support centralized, distributed, cloud-based, on-premises, or hybrid implementations and may integrate with identity-management systems, credential providers, security-monitoring tools, and authorization services.

By classifying potential users as non-users, eligible users, limited users, or authorized users and by incorporating sensitive-sector affiliation into the classification process, the invention enables access privileges to be matched more precisely to each requester’s status and need. This approach reduces unnecessary exposure of protected resources, supports consistent enforcement of security policies, and provides stronger controls for a shared data processing environment serving users with differing roles, affiliations, and risk profiles.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a method, apparatus, and computer-readable medium that processes access requests to a secure data processing center and classifies potential users by access rights.
counterfactuals.output: A method, apparatus, and non-transitory computer-readable medium are disclosed for processing access requests to a secure data processing center. An access request associated with a potential user is received and evaluated using identity information, authentication credentials, contextual data, and one or more access-control policies. Based on the evaluation, the potential user is classified into an access-rights category defining permitted resources, operations, locations, and/or access periods. The classification may account for user role, security clearance, device status, request origin, behavioral indicators, and risk score. Access to the secure data processing center is selectively granted, restricted, subjected to additional authentication, or denied in accordance with the assigned category. The classification may be dynamically updated in response to detected events or changes in contextual data. Information relating to the request, classification, and resulting access decision may be recorded in an audit log and used to generate security notifications or initiate remedial actions.
